**Sundhedsklyngen Slagelse** is a healthcare cluster (sundhedsklynge) in Denmark, operating as a local organizational unit within [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] [^src4]. It is one of the many regional clusters evaluated in the 2024 annual quality report on [[atrieflimren]] treatment published by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP). The cluster is particularly notable for meeting the national quality standard for Indicator 1, which measures the timely initiation of anticoagulation therapy in newly diagnosed patients, achieving a compliance result of 93.4% [^src1].

The RKKP report tracks the cluster's performance across a wide range of clinical quality indicators to monitor cardiovascular care and stroke prevention. Sundhedsklyngen Slagelse is evaluated on anticoagulation treatment coverage, including 1-year and 2-year coverage metrics [^src6], as well as 2-year and 5-year treatment coverage [^src2]. Furthermore, the cluster's adherence to monitoring protocols, such as annual P-creatinine measurements for patients on DOAC treatment, is assessed [^src3]. The cluster is also monitored for adverse outcomes, including the incidence of severe bleeding within one year of a new diagnosis (Indicator 11) and the incidence of heart failure within one year (Indicator 15) [^src5]. 

On a national level, the geographic distribution of ischemic stroke (apopleksi) incidence among atrial fibrillation patients is mapped across healthcare clusters. Sundhedsklyngen Slagelse is included in this analysis for [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]], which tracks stroke incidence rates to identify local variations in clinical practice and patient outcomes [^src3]. By breaking down data to the cluster level, the report enables targeted quality improvement strategies, allowing Slagelse to benchmark its performance against national standards and other local clusters such as [[sundhedsklyngen-holbaek|Sundhedsklyngen Holbæk]] and [[sundhedsklyngen-nykoebing-f|Sundhedsklyngen Nykøbing F]].
